ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (as amended by Law No. 154 of 2019); Law No. 194 of 2020 promulgating the Companies Law and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 2022); GAFI and Financial Regulatory Authority board decrees on beneficial ownership identification and UBO register maintenance; Central Bank of Egypt and Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) binding directives implementing FATF Recommendations 24 and 25.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry (e.g., Companies House, US Secretary of State, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (home-country notary → home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs → Egyptian Consulate; Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Bylaws) of the non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or certified corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (home-country notary → home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs → Egyptian Consulate)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC, appointment of directors/general manager, and approval of capital remittance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary of the foreign shareholder, notarized in the home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (home-country notary → home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs → Egyptian Consulate)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization where required by the receiving Egyptian bank (home-country notary → home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs → Egyptian Consulate); otherwise notarized original accepted under the receiving bank's customer due diligence policy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI list, MENAFATF regional notices, and the Egyptian domestic terrorism-financing list published by the EMLCU/Office of the Attorney General. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by any PEP designation, sanctions hit, adverse media, or high-risk jurisdiction nexus; PEP status within 12 months of exit from public office remains an EDD trigger. CDD documentation must be refreshed every 36 months or upon any change of ownership. Banking counterparties will additionally apply FATF International Co-operation Review Group risk weighting to Egyptian-structured clients; any grey-list or black-list status at the time of deposit will elevate the 'Low_Risk_Standard' classification to enhanced monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) e-services portal at https://www.gafi.gov.eg, integrated with the Commercial Registry database of the Ministry of Trade and Industry (Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The trade name of an Egyptian LLC must be expressed in Arabic; the Arabic name governs for registry, tax, and judicial purposes. A foreign-language (e.g., English) name may be registered only as a transliteration or complementary version and must not conflict with the Arabic name or misrepresent the corporate form. The name must include the company's object and may include the Arabic LLC suffix (شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة) or its common abbreviation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Insurance, Reinsurance, Finance (requires Central Bank of Egypt or FRA licensing)
Petroleum, Gas, Oil, Mining (requires Ministry of Petroleum licensing)
Military, Defense, Security, Intelligence (requires Ministry of Defense approval)
Egypt, Arab Republic, Presidential, Government, National, Federal (misleading state affiliation; requires special authorization)
International, Global, Holdings (requires substantive qualifying grounds)
Foundation, Association, Non-Governmental Organization (inconsistent with LLC legal form)
Vocabulary identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered trademark or GAFI-registered company name
Islamic or religious denomination terms where the business plan does not evidence Sharia-compliant operations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reservation may be renewed via the GAFI portal for one additional 30-day cycle within the initial window. If the name is rejected: (1) file a formal administrative objection with the GAFI Legal Affairs Sector within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching trademark coexistence evidence or a script-diacritic/similarity analysis; (2) upon a second rejection, elevate the matter to the GAFI Grievance Committee within 60 days of the first decision; (3) after exhaustion of administrative remedies, initiate judicial review before the competent administrative court (State Council) within 60 days of the grievance decision; alternatively, propose a modified and substantively different name and re-initiate the reservation workflow without penalty.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a mail-only or pure virtual address. The LLC must maintain a physical registered seat in Egypt for service of process, statutory records inspection, and tax correspondence. A managed-office or shared business-center arrangement providing a dedicated physical desk, signage, mail collection, and meeting-room access is market-standard for a MedTech regulatory consulting practice and is accepted by GAFI and the Egyptian Tax Authority as adequate commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximately 8-12% probability of an unannounced physical verification visit within the first 24 months (commercial registry and Egyptian Tax Authority field audits). The risk declines to <5% annually for low-risk consulting LLCs after one clean fiscal year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018), Executive Regulations of Law 159/1981, Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Articles 94-125 govern Limited Liability Companies, supplemented by the GAFI One-Stop-Shop procedural rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop-Shop (OSS), Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade; Commercial Registry (Al-Sijil Al-Tijari) for enrollment.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Contract (Memorandum of Association - Aqd Al-Sharika) in Arabic, notarized by the Notary Public and filed electronically through the GAFI One-Stop-Shop portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Egyptian LLC has no express statutory minimum capital; however, the capital must be divided into equal quotas with a nominal value not less than EGP 100 (or more as set in the Company Contract) and must be sufficient to achieve the corporate objects. The paid-up portion must be deposited into a temporary capital subscription escrow account at a licensed Egyptian bank, and the bank-issued Capital Deposit Certificate must be submitted to GAFI. Non-resident ownership is permitted; in-kind contributions require independent valuation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole founding manager of the LLC, having reviewed the Company Contract notarized on the date of incorporation, subscribes fully to the Company's share capital and confirms that the paid-up portion has been deposited in the Company's temporary escrow bank account, the capital deposit certificate being filed herewith. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company situated in the Arab Republic of Egypt is adopted as the official seat and address for service of process, with statutory registers and corporate seal kept there. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Founding Manager appoints the Managing Director and the Compliance Officer named in the Company Contract, with authority, jointly or singly, to complete Commercial Registry enrollment, tax registration, social insurance registration, and opening of the Company's bank account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (OSS) National Online Platform - Company Name Reservation Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the GAFI OSS online platform and access the Company Name Reservation module. File a name reservation request listing up to three proposed Arabic and English names in priority order; the system performs an automated conflict search against the Commercial Registry database and reserves the first available name for a period of 60 days. Pay the name reservation fee online and download the Name Reservation Certificate, which is mandatory for all subsequent notarization and incorporation filings.
required_dossiers: Passport copies or national ID copies of all founding shareholders and managers
Three proposed company names in Arabic and English
Initial managerial resolution authorizing the name reservation application
Power of attorney if the application is filed through a licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name conflicts with an existing Commercial Registry entry, GAFI issues a rejection notice with the conflicting details; the applicant may file an administrative appeal and resubmit with alternative names within 10 working days without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Offices (Tawtheeq), Ministry of Justice; alternatively the notary desk within the GAFI OSS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders or their duly authorized attorneys must appear before the Notary Public with the draft Company Contract in Arabic. The contract must state the LLC name, registered office, objects, capital divided into equal quotas, distribution of quotas among shareholders, appointment of managers, and duration. Pay the notarization fee, stamp duties, and capital-based contract stamp duty. Obtain the authenticated notarized deed, which is the foundational incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Draft Company Contract signed in ink by each founding shareholder
GAFI Company Name Reservation Certificate
Valid national ID or passport of each founding shareholder and manager
Consular legalization of signatures for foreign signatories
Power of attorney for any authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary Public raises rectification comments, such as omitted capital provisions, insufficient stamp duty, or incomplete identity documents, the applicant must execute a corrective notarial deed or supplementary contract within 5 working days, pay the differential stamp duty, and resubmit the file for notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-Up Capital Deposit and Escrow Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed Egyptian commercial bank - Capital Deposit Desk under the Head Office KYC/AML Compliance Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized Company Contract to the chosen bank and open a temporary capital subscription escrow account in the name of the LLC. Transfer the paid-up capital from the shareholders' accounts via bank wire or cash deposit; the bank verifies the identity of all depositors and the source of funds in accordance with Egyptian AML/CFT regulations. Upon confirmation, the bank issues the official Capital Deposit Certificate evidencing the deposited paid-up capital, which is a mandatory attachment to the GAFI incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Notarized Company Contract (certified true copy)
GAFI Name Reservation Certificate
Valid passport or national ID of each shareholder and the authorized manager
Bank account opening application and AML/KYC questionnaire
Corporate economic substance declaration for non-resident shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's AML/KYC review requires clarification of the source of funds, the applicant must provide a certified declaration, supporting bank statements, or a formal wealth confirmation letter. In the case of a currency discrepancy, the difference must be re-deposited, and an amended Capital Deposit Certificate will be issued within 2 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Statutory Incorporation Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (OSS) - Incorporation Division, Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic incorporation application through the GAFI OSS portal by uploading the notarized Company Contract, Capital Deposit Certificate, Name Reservation Certificate, valid identity documents of shareholders and managers, and the registered-office lease or free-use agreement. Pay the official state registration fee (approximately USD 250 equivalent, payable in EGP). Upon substantive review and approval, GAFI issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Wathiqat Al-Taw'id), assigns the preliminary Commercial Registration Number, and automatically forwards the file to the Commercial Registry for enrollment.
required_dossiers: Notarized Company Contract (original notarial copy)
Bank Capital Deposit Certificate
GAFI Name Reservation Certificate
Passport or national ID of each shareholder and manager
Registered-office lease contract or ownership title or gratis license
Power of attorney if filing through a corporate agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query letter, the applicant must respond in writing with all corrective documents within 15 days. Minor deficiencies may be cured by amending the Company Contract or supplementing the bank certificate; if the applicant fails to respond, GAFI may reject the file, requiring a fresh submission with the original fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Enrollment and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office (within GAFI OSS) and Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Tax Card and VAT Registration Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Commercial Registry enrollment to obtain the final Commercial Registry Extract confirming the legal existence and authorized signatories of the LLC. Simultaneously file with the Egyptian Tax Authority the applications for the Tax Card (Kart Dahribi), VAT and e-invoice registration, payroll withholding tax stamp duty registration, and tax certificate for the registered office address. Provide the electronic signature token details of the authorized manager for the ETA online filing portal.
required_dossiers: GAFI Certificate of Incorporation
Notarized Company Contract
Approved registered-office lease contract
Manager national ID and specimen signature
ETA Tax Card application form (Form 001)
Company seal impression and list of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Commercial Registry deficiency notices are cured by producing the GAFI incorporation file and paying the nominal rectification fee; ETA queries on the office address are cured by presenting the Civil Defense safety approval and a municipal inspection certificate; late registration penalties may apply if the statutory timeline is exceeded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Seal, and Physical Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior), Local Municipal Unit, Social Insurance Authority (NIO), Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first statutory meeting of the founders and pass the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution adopting the registered office, confirming share subscription, and appointing the Managing Director and Compliance Officer. Procure the mandatory Civil Defense fire-safety certificate for the rented office, obtain the building structural load and occupancy clearance from the local municipality, produce the official company seal through the licensed notary procedure, register the founding manager and any employees with the Social Insurance Authority using Form 1/2, and apply for the compulsory membership certificate from the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce.
required_dossiers: Signed Pro-Forma First Board Resolution minutes
Office lease contract and municipal office permit
Civil Defense inspection request form
Social Insurance Authority enrollment Form 1/2 and payroll schedule
Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce membership application
Fee payment receipts for all governmental clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Civil Defense rejection requires implementation of corrective fire-safety measures such as fire extinguishers, emergency exit signage, and proper electrical load distribution, followed by a reinspection within 10 working days; municipal structural certification objections are cured by an engineering office load assessment report; social insurance queries are cured by submission of the signed payroll register.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA), Ministry of Trade and Industry - industrial production license regime not applicable to this office-based MedTech regulatory consulting activity; only administrative physical clearances are mandatory.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Occupancy and Business Premises Permit for Commercial Offices, together with the Civil Defense Fire-Safety Certificate; no IDA industrial operating license is required for non-manufacturing consulting operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category (C) - Registration and Notification only; office-based professional consulting is exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report under Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009, and its Executive Regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by the consulting activity. Compliance obligations include municipal solid waste segregation and contracted disposal pursuant to Law No. 202 of 2020; interior ambient noise not exceeding 65 dBA during daytime commercial hours under Law No. 4 of 1994; and disposal of any office electronic waste exclusively through EEAA-licensed recycling facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory Civil Defense fire-safety certificate issued by the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) based on a physical inspection of fire extinguishers, emergency exits, electrical load, and evacuation routes; a structural load and occupancy clearance from the local municipal engineering department verifying safe floor loading; and a workplace occupational safety statement covering ventilation, wiring safe, and emergency lighting.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must appoint a local tax representative, obtain a Tax Card (Bawbata Taksit), register for corporate tax under the unified tax law, and obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN) via the ETA's e-registration portal. VAT registration is mandatory separately once the taxable turnover threshold is met.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election available. LLCs are taxed as juridical persons. Certain elections exist under the Income Tax Law (e.g., election for deemed expenses regime), but no hybrid mismatch elections are recognized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for goods and services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates e-invoicing with real-time ETA clearance through API integration. Invoices must be digitally stamped and authenticated via the ETA e-invoicing system before issuance; failure to clear invoices triggers non-deductibility and penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported to non-residents and services provided to non-resident recipients that are performed and consumed entirely outside Egypt qualify for 0% VAT. Substantiation requires evidenced physical export or offshore service delivery, supported by contracts and FX remittance records.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA may retrospectively disallow zero-rating and claw back unpaid VAT plus late interest and penalties (up to 100% of tax due) for fraudulent or improperly documented export claims. Criminal penalties may apply for deliberate evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), its implementing regulations, and CBE foreign-exchange circulars and exchange-control directives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains liberalized current-account convertibility under the CBE-managed float adopted in 2024. Payments for services, royalties, dividends, profit remittances, and commercial settlements are convertible through authorized banks when supported by underlying contracts, invoices, tax clearance, and economic-substance evidence. Capital-account transactions such as equity injections, shareholder loans, liquidation proceeds, and onward foreign investment are permitted only through CBE-licensed authorized dealers and are subject to documentary verification, balance-of-payments classification, and, in certain cases, CBE approval. Profit remittance requires audited financial statements, a tax clearance certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the LLC's board/shareholder resolution approving the distribution; no fixed annual remittance quota exists under the current regime, but CBE and the bank will independently verify the underlying distributable profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: CBE directives require exporters of goods to repatriate export proceeds through an authorized Egyptian bank within 90 days of shipment date or the documented commercial payment due date. The prevailing mandatory surrender/conversion ratio is 100% of export receipts, converted at the interbank market rate, unless CBE grants a specific retention allowance for defined operational expenses. Service exporters, including regulatory consulting providers, must similarly route international receipts through an authorized bank; the bank records the proceeds under the applicable current-account service code and applies CBE conversion requirements. Supporting evidence includes customs declarations, signed service agreements, invoices, proof of delivery of regulatory deliverables, SWIFT receipts, and bank credit advices.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Egyptian law does not recognize offshore fintech EMIs as banks, clearing institutions, or local payment-service providers. Only CBE-licensed banks and authorized exchange/payment intermediaries may hold EGP accounts, issue Egyptian IBANs, and clear SWIFT or local currency payments. Offshore EMIs cannot serve as the primary liquidity rail for inbound capital, trade settlements, or dividend remittances. They may be used only as an invoicing or payment-orchestration front end that routes funds to a licensed Egyptian bank account; using them as a standalone treasury solution presents material regulatory, sanctions, and AML risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of the LLC's legal representative, manager, and all authorized signatories is normally mandatory at the chosen Egyptian bank. Remote account opening is not generally permitted for new corporate clients, including non-resident-owned LLCs; the CBE's KYC framework requires original identity documents, corporate register extracts, and in-person verification before account activation. Non-resident directors who will act as signatories must attend in person or execute a notarized power of attorney in favor of an approved resident signatory, with all corporate documents properly legalized for use in Egypt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity through non-resident holding structures and unverified individual shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully completed CBE-compliant UBO declaration form; certified copies of passport and national ID of every shareholder at the threshold; share register and articles of association showing the full ownership chain; sworn statements confirming no nominee ownership; official Egyptian UBO register filing receipt where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inadequate or unexplained source of funds for initial capital, shareholder loans, or foreign remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of personal/corporate bank statements for the remitting entity; audited financial statements or accountant-certified financial position; tax returns and tax clearance certificates; accumulation explanation for high-net-worth shareholders; executed subscription or shareholder loan agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border service receipts that may be misclassified as export goods or lack sufficient current-account substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed consulting service agreements describing FDA 510(k) filing and CE marking deliverables; milestone reports and proof of submission to FDA or EU Notified Body; correspondence with regulators showing ongoing advisory engagement; invoices describing regulatory consulting services; bank commentary noting the applicable current-account service purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, negative media, politically exposed person (PEP) status, or adverse beneficial-ownership reputational exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and PEP screening report prepared by a recognized data provider; sworn declaration of source of wealth and source of funds; recent certificate of incumbency; professional references; detailed CV and regulatory credentials confirming the legitimate nature of the MedTech consulting business; enhanced monitoring remediation plan if a PEP or close associate is identified.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Incoming equity capital must be remitted from the shareholder's own account at a recognized foreign bank to the LLC's CBE-licensed account in Egypt. The wire must clearly state 'Capital Contribution / Equity Injection' and the LLC's Commercial Registration Number. The receiving bank requires a notarized shareholder resolution approving the capital increase, updated articles of association, and a shareholder declaration identifying the ultimate funder. The transaction is classified under the CBE balance-of-payments code for foreign direct investment in a non-bank Egyptian company, and the bank will issue an inward-investment certificate after verification. Current-account service receipts, including FDA/CE consulting fees from non-resident clients, must be routed with the applicable 'Business and Management Consulting Services' purpose code; the signed engagement letter, scoped deliverable description, and evidence of service performance must be maintained at the bank for transaction-level audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Service disbursements, such as FDA filing fees, CE technical-file review fees, and overseas legal counsel payments, should be paid by SWIFT MT103 through the LLC's authorized dealing bank using the underlying invoice and contract as clearing support. For goods-related transactions connected to medical-device pilot production or prototype acquisition, commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) may be issued through a CBE-licensed bank, while low-value, repetitive purchases may use direct MT103 remittance if the bank's transaction-monitoring rules tolerate open-account terms. All outbound payments require purpose-code declaration, invoice certification, and, where applicable, tax withholding or transfer-pricing documentation. Profit and dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders use a separate outbound MT103 after the Egyptian Tax Authority clearance and CBE current-account conversion review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards executed with a CBE-licensed authorized bank, supported by documented underlying current-account or trade exposure
Non-deliverable FX forwards (NDFs) referencing EGP for offshore hedge compression, permitted only where the counterparty is a relevant licensed financial institution and the hedge is non-speculative
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) with a CBE-licensed bank for matched medium-term capital or trade-related liabilities
FX options and structured forwards offered only by a CBE-authorized dealer, subject to execution of a non-speculation attestation and suitability assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Annual Renewal and Updated Particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, Commercial Registry Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 31 May; due each calendar year regardless of the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal is subject to a late fee under Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; continued failure beyond the renewal window permits administrative strike-off and suspension of the company's commercial status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 April following the tax year-end, or within four months after the approved fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine under EIT Law No. 91 of 2005, Articles 134 and 135, of EGP 500 to EGP 5,000; unpaid tax attracts a 2% monthly delay fee capped at 20%; enforcement collection and suspension of tax registration may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Audit Report and Shareholders' Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company head office; available on demand to GAFI, ETA and competent inspection authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the company's fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes a violation under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; responsible managers may be personally fined up to EGP 50,000, and GAFI may revoke reliance on the company's audit exemption.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Register and Shareholding Transfer Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry Office; anti-money-laundering inspectors on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Updated and confirmed at the annual commercial renewal; individual UBO changes reflected within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to record transfers or update UBO data may lead to fines under AML Law No. 80 of 2002 and refusal of the company's future notarization or registration acts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Egyptian LLC must arrange an independent audit by a certified auditor registered under Law No. 115 of 2015 unless the company qualifies as a dormant small entity expressly exempted in its incorporation contract and files no corporate tax return. In practice, a statutory audit is always required for an active LLC filing a corporate tax return, for any LLC with paid-up capital equal to or above EGP 50,000, or where the Articles of Association stipulate audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued under Law No. 115 of 2015 and Ministerial Decree No. 110 of 2015, substantially aligned with IFRS; simplified EAS for SMEs is permitted for smaller LLCs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone Egyptian UBO annual return. The manager or legal representative must certify at the Commercial Register annual renewal that the UBO register remains accurate; any share transfer must be entered in the Register of Members and reflected in the UBO register within 30 days. The register must be kept at the registered office and produced during statutory inspections.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Meetings and Manager Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 900 per year for a registered address and corporate secretarial address
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 900 – USD 2,500 per audit cycle for a small to mid-sized consulting LLC

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No targeted statutory holiday for regulatory consulting; standard deductions and investment incentives under Law 72/2017 may apply if qualifying assets are used; not automatically assumed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Form No. 10) filed via the Egyptian Tax Authority's electronic portal (E-Invoicing / Tax Return application)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 30 April for a 31 December year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Revenue: aggregate worldwide or Egypt-source revenue from FDA 510(k) filing and CE Mark compliance advisory services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers report only income effectively connected with an Egyptian permanent establishment; pure offshore services are generally outside scope unless sourced in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible Expenses: operating costs, salaries, rent, professional indemnity insurance, amortisation and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be apportioned to the Egyptian PE; foreign head-office expenses are deductible only to the extent allowed under Egyptian tax law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income: gross revenue less deductible expenses and any tax-loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents compute taxable income only from Egyptian-source amounts attributable to the PE; treaty provisions may limit the taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate Tax at 22.5%: statutory rate applied to Box 3a taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same statutory rate for PEs; no preferential rate unless a specific treaty or investment code provision applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Credits and Advance Payments: foreign tax credits, tax withheld at source by clients, and quarterly advance payments made during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim foreign tax credit for taxes paid abroad on Egyptian-source income if a DTA permits; advance payments must be reconciled in the final annual return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty equal to 3% of the tax due for each month of delay, capped at 25% of the tax; plus fixed administrative fines for failure to submit electronically.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (increased rate of 25% may apply under specific anti-abuse circumstances, not assumed)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Residency (TRC) from their home tax authority, submit a reduced withholding rate application to the Egyptian Tax Authority via the relevant form (Form 89) together with the TRC, and ensure the Egyptian payer withholds at the treaty rate prior to remittance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: royalties 20%, interest 20%. Treaty rates vary (often 15% for interest, 20% for royalties under many DTAs); applicable DTA rate prevails if TRC is filed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File required when related-party transactions exceed EGP 5 million per transaction or EGP 10 million aggregate; Master File threshold: group consolidated revenue exceeding EGP 200 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has no offshore-style ESR regime, but tax law and CFC rules require substantial business purpose; the Tax Authority may apply general anti-abuse rules to disregard entities lacking commercial substance, and Art. 119(bis) of Tax Law 91/2005 (as amended) targets controlled foreign corporations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fraudulent underreporting of service revenues, fabricating deductible invoices, or falsifying tax records for FDA/CE consulting fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to EGP 200,000 plus 100% of evaded tax; imprisonment up to 5 years; forced closure and blacklisting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly and severally liable for evaded tax if personally involved; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed; potential imprisonment for 3–5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a nominee with no staff, physical premises, or real activity, while repatriating service fees as dividends or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and tax credits; reclassification of income as taxable distribution; penalty of 30% of the reclassified amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing may lead to personal liability for unpaid withholding tax; responsible officers may face administrative fines of EGP 50,000–100,000 and possible criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting consulting fees in suspicious structuring via third-party receipts, cash splitting, or using shell bank accounts to evade AML screening.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 80/2002, imprisonment up to 15 years and fines up to EGP 500,000; asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally fined up to EGP 1,000,000 and imprisoned; travel bans and extradition possible.
